name: Kittim
overview: Kittim is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the son of Javan, as recorded in Genesis 10:4. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His mention is brief and focuses on his genealogical position within the descendants of Noah.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Kittim' appears as a proper name in Scripture, specifically in Genesis 10:4. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is indicated in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Kittim as the son of Javan, establishing a direct father-son relationship. No other family relationships or tribal connections are detailed beyond this lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Kittim's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records that trace the descendants of Noah, highlighting the spread of nations after the flood. As a son of Javan, he is part of the lineage associated with the maritime peoples, which situates him within the broader biblical narrative of the nations' origins. His mention helps to understand the ethnic and geographical expansions that Scripture outlines.
